name: Appliance repair

pf.license.need: Most states don't license appliance repair. Some register repair companies, and some cities license repair shops: the state's or city's form says. Refrigeration work and gas or electric hookups can need that trade's own license.
pf.license.who holds it: The company, where the state registers repair companies. Each tech, only for what their own card or license covers: an EPA refrigerant card for sealed systems, and a refrigeration or gas license where the state asks.
what to ask: The company's repair registration or license number, where the state's form asks for one
Each tech's EPA refrigerant card number and type, for anyone who opens a sealed system
Each tech's refrigeration or gas license, where the state's form asks, in their invite reply
A maker's authorized-servicer number, only if the business takes that maker's warranty jobs
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.renewals: Reminders before each license or registration expires, on the dates the owner picks. EPA cards don't expire. A lapsed license pauses new bookings for that person.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance, and a bond where the state's form asks for one: from the state form.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks.
pf.license.at the shop: A small-appliance repair shop: the state's or city's form says if it needs a registration. Safe default: the business registration on file, shown on the listing.
pf.license.local rules: Some cities license repair shops or home repair businesses on their own: the form for that place applies, by the customer's address.

pf.services.capacity: One tech per booking. A built-in install, or pulling a built-in fridge out, needs a crew of two. The shop's restores need its restore bench.
pf.services.skills each needs: Sealed-system work needs an EPA refrigerant card. Gas ranges, ovens and dryers need the gas skill. Built-ins need a tech cleared for them. Restores at the shop need the restore skill.
pf.services.nobody home: Never at the home: an adult (18 or older) is there for the whole visit. At the shop, a drop-off needs nobody to wait.
pf.services.online: A video check of a small appliance only, where the owner offers it. No repair is done by video.
pf.services.warranty jobs: Under the maker's warranty: the maker sends its own servicer, so Rosie points the customer there and takes nothing. Only a business the maker authorized takes them, and the owner adds that service.
pf.services.extras: Travel inside the service area only (the example: 25 miles). Parts at the owner's price, shown on the quote. No tax line unless the owner sets a rate. The business's own warranty on the receipt (the example: 90 days on parts and labor). A loaner mini fridge while a part is on order, only where the owner offers one: the customer says yes on the secure page, and the general rules for rentals set any deposit or card saved for damage.

stops the booking.words: A gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm (a gas range, oven or dryer)
stops the booking.says: Leave the house now and keep everyone out. Don't flip switches, unplug anything or use a phone inside. Once outside, call 911 and the gas company.
stops the booking.booking: No booking. A new request must say the gas company cleared the home.

stops the booking.says: Get everyone out now. Once outside, call 911. Don't go back in.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: Sparks or a burning smell from an appliance
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Unplug it, or switch off its breaker, only if that's safe. Don't use it until it's fixed.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: Water near outlets (a washer, a dishwasher, a fridge's water line)
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Stay away from wet outlets and cords. Turn off the appliance's water supply if you can reach it without touching the water.

pf.safety.at the shop: A small appliance that smoked, sparked or got wet is brought in unplugged and isn't used. A gas appliance part isn't worked on at the shop: the customer is offered a home visit by a tech with the gas skill.
pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first.

before the main visit.for: Any appliance bought in the last few years, or 'not sure'
before the main visit.timing: Before times show. 'Not sure' means the label photo is checked before the booking is confirmed.

before the main visit.for: Built-in and commercial units: special parts, and two people to pull one out

before the main visit.step: A part check (the item brought in, or its label photo)
before the main visit.for: A special-order part at the shop
before the main visit.timing: At least 2 days before; stays good 3 months

prep for the reminder: A fridge that isn't cooling: leave it plugged in and don't defrost it. The frost shows what failed. Move food to a cooler.
Clear a path to the appliance, and space to pull it out
A washer or dishwasher with water in it: leave the water in, and put towels down
At the shop: bring the appliance with all its parts, like the bowl, the lid and the cord

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's home: The check-in code at the door. The on-my-way text names the tech, with a photo.
pf.visit.check-in at the shop: The code at the counter (the tech or the desk types it). A drop-off gets its code when the item is left, and READY when it's tested.
pf.visit.quotes at the visit: The tech texts the quote with its lines before any work, and says if a part must be ordered. The customer may OK part of it. The quote stays good 7 days.
pf.visit.parts on order: A part that isn't on the van is ordered at the visit. The job stays open, the return visit is booked after the part's due date, and it adds no new service call. At the shop, the item stays until it's READY.
pf.visit.extra work: Quoted by text up to the owner's limit (the example: $500). Above it, the owner OKs it first. A bigger job found, like a sealed-system repair, gets its own quote.
pf.visit.work sold at the home: A written right to cancel, where the rules require it.
pf.visit.repair or replace: The tech gives the price. Repair or replace is the customer's call; Rosie never advises.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The tech runs the appliance with the customer, then texts DONE with the bill's lines.
pf.visit.maker's cover: From the serial, the tech checks if the maker may still cover a part, like a fridge's sealed system. If so, only the service call is owed, and the customer is sent to the maker.

starting answers: At the customer's home: a card saved for the $89 service call, credited to the repair, and Rosie texts the bill after the job

limits: Work quoted at the visit: nothing more than the service call is taken before
A deposit only on a quoted install (the example: 25%). Deposit cap: from the state form

pf.money.insurance and plans: A home warranty or store plan pays only once the owner checks it. The maker's warranty goes to the maker's own servicer. Insurance: the customer pays, and gets the receipt and the failure report for the claim.
pf.money.tax: No tax line unless the owner sets a rate where the state taxes the work or the parts.
pf.money.parts: Parts at the owner's price, on the quote. A part ordered just for the customer is billed if they cancel only if they agreed in writing before it was ordered.
pf.money.Rosfield's $2: Applies, as for every kind of work. A return visit for a part on order is the same booking.

pf.messages.never in a text: Gate or lock codes, card details, the label photo's serial number, and photos from inside the home: these stay on the secure page.
pf.messages.danger words: Gas words always get the safety message first, before anything else.

pf.staff.levels: Tech and lead tech, by the owner's own titles. A state license per person only where the state's form asks.
pf.staff.supervision: A trainee works only alongside a tech. A trainee is never sent alone, and never opens a sealed system.
pf.staff.special work: Sealed-system work only by a tech with an EPA card of the right type. Gas appliances only by people with the gas skill, and its license where the state requires one.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs fees, quotes over the limit, built-in and commercial jobs, and same-day jobs. An office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another tech with the same skills, at the same window and price. A sealed-system job only goes to another tech with an EPA card.

pf.rules.service call shown first: The service call charge shown before every visit: where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.written estimate: A written estimate before any repair, and nothing above it without the customer's OK: from the state form.
pf.rules.OK when not home: A customer who isn't home OKs the quote by text, and the OK is kept with the date, time and name: where the rules require it.
pf.rules.contract: A signed contract before work above an amount, and any days to cancel: from the state form.
pf.rules.license on papers: The registration or license number on confirmations, quotes and bills: from the state form.
pf.rules.invoice: What the bill must list, like each part and whether it's new, used or rebuilt: from the state form.
pf.rules.old parts: Replaced parts given back, unless they go back to the maker under warranty: where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.refrigerant: A sealed system is opened only by a tech with an EPA card, and the refrigerant is recovered: always.
pf.rules.warranty: The owner's own (the example: 90 days on parts and labor), shown on the receipt.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, as for every kind of work, or longer where the state's form asks.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for appliance repair:
appliance repair: Still under the maker's warranty: pointed to the maker before any time is saved; 'not sure' is checked from the label photo
A part must be ordered: the job stays open, and the return visit is booked after the due date
The part comes late: new times after the new date, or the repair is cancelled and only what was agreed is owed
A sealed-system leak: only a tech with an EPA card; the maker's longer cover is checked from the serial first
A gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm at any point: stop, get out, call 911 and the gas company
Water near outlets from a washer or dishwasher: the safety steps, then urgent
Repair or replace: the price only; the customer decides
Nobody home at the door: the no-show steps, with the owner's OK before any fee
A built-in unit: the owner's OK first, and a crew of two
At the shop: an item that can't be fixed, a part that's out of stock, or a drop-off nobody picks up
A fridge or freezer that stopped cooling isn't a danger: the soonest times show first, and the AI says to keep the doors shut and move food to a cooler
